Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 114, verses 1–6:

Explanation of the words:

A'udhu (أعوذ): i.e., I seek refuge and protection.

Bi-Rabbi al-nas (برب الناس): i.e., the Creator and Owner of mankind.

Malik al-nas (ملك الناس): i.e., the Lord, Owner and Ruler of mankind.

Ilah al-nas (إله الناس): i.e., the One truly worshipped by mankind, since there is no one worthy of worship besides Him.

Min sharr al-waswas (من شر الوسواس): i.e., from the evil of Satan; it is named by the verbal noun (al-masdar) because of his constant involvement in it.

Al-Khannas (الخناس): i.e., the one who withdraws and draws back from the heart when God the Exalted is remembered.

Fi suduur al-nas (في صدور الناس): i.e., in their hearts when they are heedless of the remembrance of God the Exalted.

Min al-jinnah wa al-nas (من الجنة والناس): i.e., from the devil among the jinn and the devil among mankind.

Meaning of the verses:

God the Exalted says: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind﴾. This surah is one of the two protective surahs (al-mu'awwidhatan): the first is al-Falaq, and this one is al-Nas. The first includes four matters from which refuge is sought: from the evil of every creature in all of creation; from the evil of what occurs in darkness, the darkness of night or the darkness of the moon when it sets; from the evil of the sorceresses who blow on knots; and from the evil of the envier when he envies. These four cover everything feared for its harm and injury. As for the surah of al-Nas, it includes one evil, but it is more dangerous than those four, because it relates to the heart, and when the heart is corrupted everything is corrupted, and when it is sound everything is sound. For this reason, the surah of al-Nas is specifically for seeking refuge from the evil of the whisperer, the withdrawing one, who whispers in the hearts of mankind, from among the jinn and mankind. So His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind﴾ is a command from Him to His Messenger, and his community follows him: "A'udhu" means I take refuge in the Lord of mankind, i.e., their Creator, Owner and God, besides whom there is no god for them, from the evil of the whisperer, who is Satan, who whispers in the hearts of mankind in a hidden voice that is not heard, casting doubts into the heart, fears and evil suspicions, adorning the ugly and making the good seem ugly. This happens whenever a person is heedless of the remembrance of God the Exalted. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿al-Khannas﴾, this is a description of the devil from the jinn, for when the servant remembers his Lord, he withdraws, i.e., he hides himself, as though he had gone away though he has not gone; and when the servant becomes heedless of the remembrance of God, he returns to whispering.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿from the jinn and mankind﴾, it means that the one who whispers to a human may be from the jinn, and may be from mankind. A human whispers in the sense of doing the work of Satan: adorning evil, beautifying the ugly, casting doubts into the soul, and stirring up thoughts and suggestions with corrupt words and misleading expressions. Indeed, the harm one human inflicts on another is greater than the harm of Satan upon a human, for the devil among the jinn is repelled by seeking refuge, whereas the devil among mankind is not repelled by it; rather, one must deal with him diplomatically and conciliate him in order to be rid of him. O God, we seek refuge in You from the evil of every evil doer, and from the evil of mankind and the jinn. So protect us, our Lord, for none protects us but You. Our Lord, to You belong praise and thanks.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The obligation of seeking refuge in God the Exalted from the devils of mankind and of the jinn.

2- Affirmation of the Lordship and Godhead of God the Exalted, Mighty and Majestic.

3- Clarification of the wording of seeking refuge, which is "A'udhu billahi min al-shaytan al-rajim", as clarified by the authentic Sunnah, when two men quarrelled in the Prophet's Mosque (al-Rawda al-Nabawiyya), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I know a word which, if this one said it, the anger would leave him, namely: A'udhu billahi min al-shaytan al-rajim."
